prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you parallel-parked a full-size pickup on the first attempt and were observed being proud about it. Respond to the committee.
response:
*rises, adjusts tie, places hand on a well-worn owner's manual*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I come before you today of my own free will, though I note the subpoena was stapled to my windshield, which frankly I consider excessive.

I will not insult this body by denying the facts. On the afternoon in question, yes, I did guide a full-size pickup — extended cab, long bed, no backup camera, may I add — into a parallel parking space on the first attempt. One motion. No pull-forward. No "close enough." The truck came to rest approximately eight inches from the curb, both ends, measured.

As to the charge of "being proud about it," I invoke no amendment. I was proud, Mr. Chairman. I stood beside that vehicle for a period of not less than ninety seconds. I placed my hands on my hips. Witnesses allege I said "yep" aloud to no one. I do not dispute this account.

You ask me: "Are you now, or have you ever been, a person who looks back at their vehicle while walking away?" 

I have, sir. Twice. Once over each shoulder.

But I want to be clear about what I will NOT do. I will not name the others. I will not tell this committee who taught me the two-wheel-rotations-then-cut-it-hard method. That man was a patriot, and he asked for nothing in return except that I check my mirrors and never, EVER trust the beeping.

If parking a truck correctly and feeling something about it is un-American, then I ask this committee — what are we even grilling for?

I yield back the remainder of my time, and I'd note for the record that my truck is parked outside. First try. Go look.
